articles.title: Import records from CSV or XLSX
articles.summary: Bring your existing data into TechSync with column mapping and duplicate detection.

body.text: Import CSV or XLSX files from the Import / export menu on Leads, Contacts, Companies or Deals. XLS files are not supported. The limit is 50,000 data rows, 200 columns and 25 MB; dense or expanded workbooks and large reviews have lower size limits and should be split.

items: Upload a file and choose the sheet and header row.
Map columns to existing fields and choose skip, update or create for duplicates. Create any needed custom fields in Settings first.
Generate the background preview. Review errors, warnings and duplicate actions. Changes to the draft require a new preview.
Confirm any skipped error rows and start. Progress and row results are saved; cancellation preserves rows already committed.

body.text: A workspace processes one preview, import or record export at a time. Other work waits. Source data pages reuse a derived copy instead of repeatedly parsing the workbook. The first file inspection still runs during upload setup.
If a job fails, review its error before resuming. Resuming uses the saved row journal. Undo is available only for eligible records that have not changed; it is not a general rollback of later work.

articles.title: Invite your team and set roles
articles.summary: Add users, choose roles and control what each person can see.

body.text: Workspace owners or members with invitation permission can invite people from Settings → Team. An invitation link expires after seven days.

Built-in roles are owner, admin, manager, sales rep and viewer. Permissions and record scopes determine each action. Custom roles can narrow modules, fields and actions; plan availability also applies.
Use search and Load more to reach members and teams beyond the first page. Assignment and owner selectors search the workspace.

articles.title: Set up your first sales pipeline
articles.summary: Choose a template, rename stages and set win probabilities.

body.text: Open Settings → Pipelines to create or edit pipelines and stages when your role allows it. Set stage names, probabilities and rotting days. On Deals, use the pipeline selector and board or list.
Moving a deal into a won or lost stage requires the applicable close details. Archived stages and pipelines are unavailable for new deals. Changes remain subject to record scope and plan limits.

articles.title: Automatically assign leads with round-robin and territory rules
articles.summary: Route new leads to the right rep the moment they arrive.

body.text: Open Settings → Assignment to configure rules and working hours. Rules are evaluated in their saved order. Search or load more to find later rules.

Supported rules select eligible members by round-robin or configured criteria. A lead can be held outside workspace working hours and released by the worker when the workspace opens. This does not infer personal leave or individual shifts.
Manual owner selection, inactive members, assignment scope and configured fallback behavior affect the result. Check the lead owner and assignment history after capture.

articles.title: Review and merge duplicate leads or contacts
articles.summary: Choose a survivor and field values before combining records.

body.text: Duplicate checks use email and phone. Select records in the Contacts list to review a contact merge. Select 2–11 non-converted leads in Leads and choose Merge to review a lead merge.

For leads, choose the surviving record and conflicting field values. Its owner and status remain. Contact points, tags, activities, tasks and supported record links are combined. Historical source records are archived with a link to the survivor. Existing deal attribution stays with each deal.

You need access to contact information and permission to edit and delete every selected lead. Converted leads, conflicting existing-contact links, busy provider operations, changed versions and oversized combined contact points or tags block the merge.
Merges cannot be undone in the app. Archived merged leads cannot be restored separately. Review the survivor and chosen field values carefully.

articles.title: Use rotting alerts to catch stalled deals
articles.summary: Highlight deals that have had no activity for too long.

body.text: Set rotting days on pipeline stages to identify open deals without recent activity. Worker scans create due alerts when configured. Check notification preferences; an alert does not guarantee an email reached an inbox.

articles.title: Enable two-factor authentication
articles.summary: Protect your account with an authenticator app.

body.text: Open Settings → Security to set up an authenticator app. Confirm the current code and save recovery codes securely. A newly enrolled factor does not create a verified sign-in session until its challenge succeeds.
If you lose access, use an unused recovery code. Do not share your authenticator secret or recovery codes.

articles.title: Export records and reports
articles.summary: Understand export scope, background jobs and private downloads.

body.text: Use Import / export for a filtered CSV or XLSX export, or select rows and use Export selected. Record exports run in the worker. Wait for completion and use the download link. Read access and the corresponding export permission are required.

Own and team exports exclude unassigned records. All-record scope includes them. This applies to record files, reports, scheduled report summaries and enabled Google Sheets exports. Contact information is blank when your role hides it.

Permissions are rebuilt during paged jobs and before publication. A later role or team change can require a fresh export; previously issued signed download links remain valid until their short expiry.

Scheduled reports show queued, preparing, sending, delivered, failed, cancelled or uncertain. Delivered means the mail server accepted the message. Failed attempts can retry safely; uncertain sends require operator review to avoid duplicates. A missing worker or unavailable SMTP can delay delivery.

articles.title: Form retries and repeat enquiries
articles.summary: Retry a failed submission without losing a genuine new enquiry.

body.text: The hosted form keeps the same request ID while retrying unchanged answers in the current page session. Within 24 hours, the same ID and answers return the earlier result without counting another enquiry. Changed answers receive a new request ID.

A new request ID or a legacy submission without one remains a separate enquiry, even if its email or phone matches an existing lead. Reloading or opening another tab can create a new ID. Retry protection is not a permanent ban on repeat enquiries.
A form that has since closed or changed its consent or origin rules can reject a retry. If the result remains unclear, check the captured lead before submitting again.
